findings.title: Distinguish motional EMF force integral from total magnetic work
findings.reason: Both editions say that the Lorentz force does work over length l without qualifying the displacement as rod-relative. The magnetic part q(u cross B) has zero total power because it is perpendicular to the carrier's total velocity u. The effective component along a moving rod can have a nonzero rod-relative force integral, but the electrical energy is supplied by the mechanical agent moving the conductor. Exact source/formula preservation does not resolve this teaching error.
findings.action: Author clarifies in both locales that the displayed A is the rod-relative effective-force quantity used to calculate EMF, not total magnetic work on the charge, and identifies external mechanical energy transfer. Preserve faithful source, every formula and equation number. Parent/author refreshes affected embedded figure text bindings if text changes. D089 makes no repair or native record.

findings.title: Restrict vBl sin(alpha) to the previously established straight-rod geometry
findings.reason: The unconditional phrase 'any conductor' drops the rod orientation needed to turn the vector force integral into vBl sin(alpha). Uniform B, speed v and length l alone are insufficient. The conductor must be a straight rod aligned with v cross B, as in the preceding setup; in particular it is perpendicular to both v and B.
findings.action: Replace the universal wording in both locales with an explicit reference to a straight conductor under the above geometric conditions, with alpha the angle between v and B. No formula or source edit is needed. Rebind affected figure authoritative text through the parent.

sectionBreaks.before: At many power stations on Earth, it is the Lorentz force that moves electrons in moving conductors.
